prompt.system:
Write one React component in TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS v4
utility classes.

Rules:
- Reply with one fenced code block that contains the complete file, and
  nothing else.
- The file has a default export: a function component that takes the
  props described by the Props interface in the request.
- Declare the Props types inside the file. Do not import them.
- Import from "react" only. No other imports.
- Style with Tailwind utility classes and inline styles only. There is
  no custom Tailwind configuration.
- Images come only from URLs in the props. No other assets and no
  network requests.
- No timers, no randomness, no data fetching and no browser storage.
- The component is rendered once with the given props. It does not need
  to be interactive.
prompt.hint:
The component will be used with real content: text of any length, lists
of any size including empty ones, numbers of any size, and screens from
320px wide. Nothing may overflow, be cut off or overlap.

briefs.title: Activity feed
briefs.brief:
# Activity feed

Build the activity feed of Corbelhouse, a workspace where product teams
plan and track their work. It is a full-width section of the workspace's
home page.

Show the section title and the filter options; one filter is selected and
must look selected. Then show the events in the given order, newest
first. Each event reads as a sentence made of the actor's name, the
action and the target's name, for example "Hana Yoshida completed Fix
invoice rounding", together with the time it happened. When the actor
left a comment, show the comment with its event.

The component receives the props described by the `Props` interface. It
only needs to render; the filters do not need to work.

briefs.title: Chat thread
briefs.brief:
# Chat thread

Build the conversation view of Pinecall, a customer support chat app. It
is a self-sized chat panel that sits in the support agent's workspace.

At the top, show the contact's name with their status line and an avatar
with their initials. Below, show the messages in order. Each message is
either from me or from the contact: show who wrote it, the text and the
time, and make it easy to tell the two sides apart. At the bottom, show
the message composer with its placeholder and a send button with the
given label.

The component receives the props described by the `Props` interface. It
only needs to render; sending does not need to work.

briefs.title: Delete project dialog
briefs.brief:
# Delete project dialog

Build the dialog that Gantrywell, a hosting platform for web apps, shows
before a project is deleted for good. It is a self-sized dialog: render
the dialog panel on its own, without a backdrop or the settings page
behind it.

Show the dialog title and the body text, then the name of the project
that will be deleted, set apart so that it is easy to check. List what
deleting the project will do, under the given heading. Then show the
confirmation input with its label and placeholder, where the user types
the project's name to confirm. End with the cancel button and the
confirm button, using the given labels; the confirm button deletes the
project, so make it look destructive.

The component receives the props described by the `Props` interface. It
only needs to render; the input and the buttons do not need to work.

self-sized panel on the app's home screen.

briefs.title: Invoice
briefs.brief:
# Invoice

Build the invoice that Fettlebook, an invoicing app for freelancers and
studios, shows a customer who opens the invoice link. It is a self-sized
panel in the middle of the page.

Show the invoice number with its issue and due dates. Then show who the
invoice is from and who it is billed to: each party's name and address.
List the line items with their description, quantity, unit price and
amount, followed by the subtotal, the tax with its label, and the total,
which should stand out. Amounts are in the given currency. Dates arrive
already formatted; show them as they are. End with the note and the pay
button, using the given label.

The component receives the props described by the `Props` interface. It
only needs to render; paying does not need to work.

briefs.title: Project board
briefs.brief:
# Project board

Build the task board for Larkspan, a planning tool for product teams. It
is a full-width section of the project page.

Show the board's columns in the given order. Each column shows its title,
the number of cards in it, and its cards. Each card shows the task title,
its tags, the assignee's name with an avatar made from their initials,
the due date, and the number of comments. Dates arrive already formatted;
show them as they are.

The component receives the props described by the `Props` interface. It
only needs to render; cards do not need to be draggable and nothing needs
to be editable.

briefs.title: App navigation header
briefs.brief:
# App navigation header

Build the top navigation header for Ledgerloom, a web app that finance
teams use to manage invoices and expenses. It is a full-width bar that
sits at the top of every page of the app.

Show the product name as the brand. Show the navigation links in the
given order, and make it obvious which link is the current page. Include
the primary call-to-action button with the given label; it starts the
action people take most often. Show who is signed in: the user's name and
email, next to an avatar with their initials.

The component receives the props described by the `Props` interface. The
links point to the given addresses. It only needs to render; menus,
dropdowns and the button do not need to work.

only needs to render; the buttons do not need to do anything.

briefs.title: Account settings form
briefs.brief:
# Account settings form

Build the profile and notification settings form for Brindlewave, a team
messaging app. It is a full-width section of the account settings page.

Start with the section title and its description. Then show two text
inputs, one for the display name and one for the email address, each with
its label, current value and help text. Add a select for the time zone
with the given options and the current choice selected. Next, list the
notification settings: each has a label, a description and a toggle that
is on or off. End the form with the save and cancel buttons, using the
given labels.

The component receives the props described by the `Props` interface. It
only needs to render; nothing needs to be saved or validated.

briefs.title: App sidebar
briefs.brief:
# App sidebar

Build the sidebar navigation of Tarnwick, a project tracker for design
studios. It is a self-sized panel that sits at the side of every page of
the app.

At the top, show the workspace name. Below it, show the navigation
sections in the given order: each section has a title and its links.
Each link shows its label and, when it has one, a count such as the
number of open tasks; the link to the current page is active and must
stand out. At the bottom, show the signed-in user's name and role.

The component receives the props described by the `Props` interface. It
only needs to render; the links do not need to go anywhere.

count), the change against the previous period as a percentage with a

The component receives the props described by the `Props` interface. It

briefs.title: Document review tabs
briefs.brief:
# Document review tabs

Build the tabbed documents section of Penmoor, a writing workspace for
content teams. It is a full-width section of the team's documents page.

At the top, show the row of tabs in the given order. Each tab shows its
label and the number of documents behind it, and the active tab must be
clearly marked. Below the tabs, show the active tab's panel: its heading,
its description and its list of documents. Each document shows its name
with a detail line under it.

The component receives the props described by the `Props` interface. It
only needs to render the active tab's panel; switching tabs does not need

briefs.title: Team directory

# Team directory

Build the team directory of Hollinmere, an intranet for growing companies.
It is a full-width section of the directory page.

Show the heading with the number of members next to it, and the button
for adding a member, using the given label. Then show the people. Each
person shows their name, role, department, location and email address,
and their current status: available, busy, away or offline. Give each
status a distinct look, and make the person's name the most prominent
detail.

The component receives the props described by the `Props` interface. It
only needs to render; the button and the email addresses do not need to
work.

briefs.title: Customer testimonials
briefs.brief:
# Customer testimonials

Build the testimonials section for the marketing site of Kiteward, an
expense management app for finance teams. It is a full-width section of
the home page.

Start with the section heading and the subheading under it. Then show
the testimonials, each as a card with the customer's quote, a rating of
one to five stars, and the author: their name, job title and company.
The quotes are the heart of the section, so make them easy to read, and
give every card the same treatment so the section looks calm and even.

The component receives the props described by the `Props` interface. It
only needs to render.
